For proof notes, tables\n   *are* the ledgers. **Fix: tables are displayable — reproduce as tables; a `LEDGER` field\n   for note-level ledger tables.**\n4. **No negative-import / non-edge field.** The §1 \"not needed\" fence and the C3-B-law\n   exclusion are the note's anti-dependency declarations. **Fix: `NON-IMPORTS` field.**\n5. **XREF designations unverified.** 7 of 22 rows point at designations absent from (or\n   mislocated in) the target note. **Fix: every XREF must be grep-verified in the target\n   file and the run must print the verification; unverifiable pointers must be emitted as\n   `DESCRIPTIVE (unverified)` or as open-obligation rows — never as bare designations.**\n6. **Consumer-designation edges dropped** (the 7 GENTOW5 chain units). **Fix: every source\n   designation appearing in a quoted statement must appear in the consumption table.**\n\n### 4.3 CHANGES the 0a charge template needs before the sweep fires (9)\n\n1. Add the `DERIVATION` field (4.2#1) — the single highest-value change.\n2. Replace the type enum (4.2#2).\n3. Add `NON-IMPORTS`, and a `LEDGER` rule for tables (4.2#3, #4).\n4. **XREF verification protocol** (4.2#5): grep-verify in target; mark unverified explicitly.\n5. **Add a TEETH INVENTORY section** — the inverse table (battery row → guarded EFF-IDs →\n   disposition ∈ {Lean theorem, executable regression, signed non-applicability}), as the\n   node schema already requires.\n6. **Header field rewrite:** \"effective-text rule — quote it if the acceptance record states\n   one; otherwise DERIVE it and state the two facts that fix it (the round's own replacement\n   instruction + the acceptance chronology)\". T3 had no literal rule and probably most notes\n   don't; the current wording pushed the compiler into a spurious open call.\n7. **Add a SCOPE-OF-RECORD block with a mandatory two-predicate split**: (i) the note's own\n   mathematical claim set (its boxed/tagged absorption or theorem list), (ii) the\n   consumption/append-protocol scope. The pilot's one substantive error came from collapsing\n   these. Require the compiler to quote the note's own boxed scope display first.\n8. **Require external-record checks before opening a scope call**: the absorbed notes' dated\n   appends and `docs/SIMPLIFICATION_BLUEPRINT_2026-08-10.md` §5.3 are in-repo and would have\n   closed OPEN-CALLs 2, 3, 4, 5 at compile time. Name these files in the charge.\n9. **Quoting hygiene**: no terminal-punctuation edits inside quoted displays; truncation only\n   with an explicit ellipsis; preserve the note's quote characters.\n\n### 4.4 Cost projection for the sweep\n\nPilot: 36,072 B source → 47,814 B spec = **1.33×**, 31 statements at ~1.54 KB/statement, on\nthe corpus's **smallest** note.\n\nAnchor density varies by an order of magnitude, and this is the load-bearing fact for sizing\n(measured `\\tag{` per KB): T3 0.72 · T1 0.31 · T2 0.15 · GENIND 0.06 · **GRTJB 0.00 · HE7\n0.00 · GENTOW5_PROOF 0.00**. T3 is the *tagged-display genre* (every load-bearing statement\ncarries a `\\tag`), which is exactly why \"quote the tagged display\" worked. The big prose\nproofs anchor on §-headers and bold `LEMMA/THEOREM` instead (GRTJB: 4 named theorems\nJB-DEV/VTX/TREE/CREAD + a §0M CONDITIONALITY MATRIX, 187 declaration keywords, 18 headers;\nHE7: 448 declaration keywords). **The pilot therefore validates the format only on the\ntagged genre — roughly 40% of corpus bytes — and gives no evidence on statement-boundary\nchoice in untagged prose notes, where \"resolve, never invent\" is under real strain.**\n\nCorpus (the design doc's 26-note list, resolved to 28 files): **2.97 MB**, of which T3 is\n36 KB. Projection at genre-differentiated ratios (≈1.3× for compressed T-units, ≈0.4–0.6×\nfor prose proofs): **≈1.3–2.2 MB of spec text, ≈350–600k output tokens** across the sweep.\n\nPer-run feasibility: 13 of the 28 files exceed 100 KB; a 240 KB note is ~70k input tokens\nplus 60–140 KB of output. Combined with the known ~10-minute external kill on codex runs\n(memory: >8 min needs nohup+disown), **single runs stay feasible only up to ~80 KB** (14\nfiles). Recommended shape:\n\n| Band | Files | Runs each | Total runs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| < 80 KB (T3, T4, T5, W11, HMENU3, HEX3, GENTOW1/3/4, HETOW, SIGMALAW, GENTOW5_WI, GENTOW6_PROOF, HE6, HE6R1) | ~15 | 1 | ~15 |\n| 80–160 KB (GENTOW2, GENTOW6_BOXES, WELDMASTER, HE3, GENTOW5_PROOF, GENH4, LIFTCORNER, GENHN, W12, HE7) | ~10 | 2–3 (by §) | ~25 |\n| > 160 KB (T1 200 K, GENIND 223 K, GRTJB 240 K, GRTJC 217 K) | ~4 | 3–4 | ~14 |\n| T2 (433 K) | 1 | 5–6 + merge | ~6 |\n\n**≈55–65 codex runs, not 25** — with a per-note header/resolution-rules run first (cheap,\nfixes the supersession theory once) and a merge/renumber pass per sharded note. Sharding is\nby the note's own § structure, with a shared EFF-ID prefix and a final cross-shard XREF\nreconciliation. Budget note: the codex 7-day window was at 61% with a Tue 2026-08-18 reset,\nso a 60-run sweep almost certainly straddles the reset — sequence the tagged T-units and the\nDAG-critical notes (T1, T2, GENTOW5_PROOF, W12) before the cap and the long prose proofs\nafter it.\n\n---\n\n## VERDICT\n\n**Sweep-readiness: GO-WITH-TEMPLATE-CHANGES (9)** — the charge template needs §4.3's nine\nchanges, and the pilot spec itself needs the four codex-revision fixes (layer 1.2 items 1–2,\nthe EFF.T3.28 truncation, the 7 XREF rows, and the scope-record split of OPEN-CALLs 3/5).\nThe compilation is otherwise sound: the one supersession in the note is resolved correctly,\n88/96 quotations are byte-verbatim, the battery is fully consumed, and the self-audit\nhonestly surfaced the one call it should not have made alone.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"10e39eed-a295-4476-831d-ad9155afb646","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/data/users/asvin/math-and-lean/p-adic-splitting-densities","sessionId":"525d9ffc-306a-4fb7-9383-b6b9ffb89267","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"main","slug":"abundant-discovering-stallman"}

(i) The branch split is not \"triply tangent vs. one genre\" but \"no\n386\t> simple residual root vs. simple residual root\"; the no-simple-root side is exactly\n387\t> {residually irreducible} ∪ {residually a perfect cube} (`cubic_trichotomy`). What survives from this section unchanged: the branch-(i)\n390\t> Taylor computation, and the naming of `cert_of_not_tang` / `decidedAt_of_not_tang` /\n391\t> `class_pinned` / `undecidedCount_le` as the `n = 2` machinery being generalised.\n392\t\n393\t**Verdict in one line: the pinning ARITHMETIC generalises cleanly and gives drainage, but a single\n394\t`class_pinned` analogue is FALSE at `n = 3`; two branches are needed, and the second branch is\n395\tblocked on a Hensel *coprime-factorisation* lemma that neither `leanfinal` nor (readily) Mathlib\n396\tprovides.**\n397\t\n398\t**What `n = 2` does** (the precise statements, not a gesture: `Drainage.cert_of_not_tang`,\n399\t`Drainage.decidedAt_of_not_tang`, `Drainage.class_pinned`, `Drainage.undecidedCount_le`)."}]},"uuid":"03372164-c91b-4b19-852a-f5db8a09cec9","timestamp":"2026-08-13T22:59:22.310Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/data/users/asvin/math-and-lean/p-adic-splitting-densities/leancheck/notes/N3_CHECK_2026-08-13.md","content":"has a level-`N+1` subclass certified `≠ σ`); all six Part-1 families are certified with exactly\ntheir claimed types (an independent check on the `(e,f)` ordering convention of §3 and on the\n`AniK`-sign bookkeeping); and no squarefree-residue class is left undecided.\n\n### 6d. ⚠ A reconciliation item for the corpus side (reported, not resolved)\n\nThe decider's TOTAL undecided count does not agree with HEX3's `U₃^conv(q,N) = q·u(q,N)`; e.g. at\n`p = 2, N = 7` the corpus value 11 328 EXCEEDS the decider's 11 264. This is **not** by itself a\ncontradiction — HEX3.B itself asserts `U₃^σ ≤ U₃^conv`, i.e. the conservative reader over-counts\nby design, and this decider is a sharper reader, so both are upper bounds on the true undecided\ncount and the corpus's being larger is expected. What it does mean is that the two numbers are\n**not measuring the same set**, so these runs neither confirm nor refute THEOREM HEX3.A. Two\nfurther data points, recorded as found and NOT tuned: (i) restricted to the triple-root branch\n(residue `= (X−ρ)³`) the decider's count equals `u(q,N)` exactly at `N = 2, 3` for both `q = 2, 3`\n(4, 16 and 9, 81) but departs at `N = 1` and at `N = 4`, where the corpus's extra term\n`(q−1)²q³` is absent because this decider certifies those classes; (ii) the complementary branch\n(residue `= (X−ρ)²(X−τ)`) contributes exactly `q(q−1)·q^{2N−2}` undecided classes in every case\ncomputed. Reconciling the two readers' conventions (per-centre vs whole-space, and the\n`B₀ = 0 in-window ⟹ UNDECIDED` exit) is a task for whoever next touches HEX3; nothing in this\nunit depends on it.\n\n---\n\n## 7. `class_pinned` AT `n = 3` — THE FEASIBILITY VERDICT (reconnaissance)\n\n> ⚠ **SUPERSEDED 2026-08-13 by unit N3B — read §9.1 and §9.4 instead.** This section's central\n> diagnosis, *\"branch (ii) is blocked on a Hensel coprime-factorisation lemma\"*, is **WRONG**,\n> as `leanfinal/notes/HENSEL_FACT_2026-08-13.md` §4.5/§7 first suspected and as §9.1 below now\n> proves: the residual shape `(X − ρ̄)(X − c̄)²` has a SIMPLE root `ρ̄`, so the ordinary ROOT form\n> of Hensel peels it, and §9.2's `decidedAt_of_peel` closes branch (ii) with no loss of level.\n> Two further corrections. (i) The branch split is not \"triply tangent vs. one genre\" but \"no\n> simple residual root vs. simple residual root\"; the no-simple-root side is exactly\n> {residually irreducible} ∪ {residually a perfect cube} (`cubic_trichotomy`). (ii) The tool the\n> REMAINING branch is short of is **strong Hensel** (`v(F(γ)) > 2v(F′(γ))` with `v(F′(γ)) > 0`),\n> NOT the factorisation form — see §9.4. What survives from this section unchanged: the branch-(i)\n> Taylor computation, and the naming of `cert_of_not_tang` / `decidedAt_of_not_tang` /\n> `class_pinned` / `undecidedCount_le` as the `n = 2` machinery being generalised.\n\n**Verdict in one line: the pinning ARITHMETIC generalises cleanly and gives drainage, but a single\n`class_pinned` analogue is FALSE at `n = 3`; two branches are needed, and the second branch is\nblocked on a Hensel *coprime-factorisation* lemma that neither `leanfinal` nor (readily) Mathlib\nprovides.**\n\n**What `n = 2` does** (the precise statements, not a gesture: `Drainage.cert_of_not_tang`,\n`Drainage.decidedAt_of_not_tang`, `Drainage.class_pinned`, `Drainage.undecidedCount_le`).","numLines":45,"startLine":355,"totalLines":785}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b69dcc4d-ac7e-4763-baf0-f1fb051d34b9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/data/users/asvin/math-and-lean/p-adic-splitting-densities","sessionId":"525d9ffc-306a-4fb7-9383-b6b9ffb89267","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"main","slug":"abundant-discovering-stallman"}

Reading the Newton polygon of `(B₀, B₁, B₂, 1)`:\n613\t\n614\t| polygon | verdict | tool status |\n615\t|---|---|---|\n616\t| `v(B₀) = 1` | Eisenstein, `{(3,1)}` | HAVE (`typeOf_ram3_of_eisenstein`) — but needs typeOf SHIFT-invariance to use at `c ≠ 0` |\n617\t| `v(B₀) = t ≢ 0 (3)`, single side | `e = 3`, `{(3,1)}` | provable by the same norm route (`CertRam3`, not landed) |\n618\t| single side of INTEGRAL slope `m` | rescale `X = π^m Y`, recurse on the residual cubic | needs typeOf SCALE-invariance |\n619\t| **two or three sides** | a root of `F` in `O` whose derivative is NOT a unit | **BLOCKED: needs STRONG HENSEL** |\n620\t\n621\t**The blocking tool is strong Hensel, not the factorization form.** Precisely: `F` monic with\n622\t`v(F(x₀)) > 2·v(F′(x₀)) = 2w`, `w ≥ 1` ⟹ `∃ r, F(r) = 0 ∧ v(r − x₀) > w`. Two observations\n623\trecorded for the next unit:\n624\t\n625\t* mathlib has this only for `ℤ_[p]` (`hensels_lemma` in `NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean`), not\n626\t  for a general complete DVR; `HenselianLocalRing.is_henselian` is the `w = 0` case only.\n627\t* **`Uniformity.Hensel.exists_monic_factorization` does NOT supply it.** After recentring, the\n628\t  residual factorization is `X · X²`, which is not coprime; and the scalings that separate the\n629\t  polygon sides are non-integral, so no monic model exists to feed the factorization form. Reading the Newton polygon of `(B₀, B₁, B₂, 1)`:\n\n| polygon | verdict | tool status |\n|---|---|---|\n| `v(B₀) = 1` | Eisenstein, `{(3,1)}` | HAVE (`typeOf_ram3_of_eisenstein`) — but needs typeOf SHIFT-invariance to use at `c ≠ 0` |\n| `v(B₀) = t ≢ 0 (3)`, single side | `e = 3`, `{(3,1)}` | provable by the same norm route (`CertRam3`, not landed) |\n| single side of INTEGRAL slope `m` | rescale `X = π^m Y`, recurse on the residual cubic | needs typeOf SCALE-invariance |\n| **two or three sides** | a root of `F` in `O` whose derivative is NOT a unit | **BLOCKED: needs STRONG HENSEL** |\n\n**The blocking tool is strong Hensel, not the factorization form.** Precisely: `F` monic with\n`v(F(x₀)) > 2·v(F′(x₀)) = 2w`, `w ≥ 1` ⟹ `∃ r, F(r) = 0 ∧ v(r − x₀) > w`. Two observations\nrecorded for the next unit:\n\n* mathlib has this only for `ℤ_[p]` (`hensels_lemma` in `NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean`), not\n  for a general complete DVR; `HenselianLocalRing.is_henselian` is the `w = 0` case only.\n* **`Uniformity.Hensel.exists_monic_factorization` does NOT supply it.** After recentring, the\n  residual factorization is `X · X²`, which is not coprime; and the scalings that separate the\n  polygon sides are non-integral, so no monic model exists to feed the factorization form. The\n  factorization form remains the right tool for `n ≥ 4` (two repeated residual blocks), as its\n  own note says — it is simply not what the `n = 3` triple-root branch is short of.\n* degree 2 escapes this because `F(γ + π^w y)/π^{2w}` is monic when `deg F = 2`\n  (`typeOf_of_certSplit`'s trick); at degree 3 the same division leaves leading coefficient\n  `π^w`, i.e. a NON-MONIC polynomial with a simple residual root — the general statement mathlib\n  also lacks. Strong Hensel and non-monic Hensel are the same missing lemma.\n\nOnce strong Hensel exists, the triple-root branch closes by the recursion\n`u(N) ≤ q^{−N/2} + q^{−5}·u(N − 3)` (each round consumes three digits of level and pins the\ncentre), which gives drainage; that estimate is written out here so the next unit can check it\nagainst its own bookkeeping, but it is NOT proved.\n\n---\n\n## 10. At `n = 3` the analogue is\n   the Taylor expansion of the recentred cubic, and the families are keyed by the Newton polygon\n   of the recentred polynomial — expect three or four families per type instead of one.\n3. **Do NOT plan on a symmetry argument.** The split/inert symmetry at `n = 2` was obtained by\n   evaluating both sides, not by an involution; at `n = 3` the analogous coincidences (e.g. the\n   two `(1,1)+(1,2)` vs `(1,3)` families) should likewise be *computed*, not matched.\n4. **The residue-field input generalises to a counting problem, not a structure theorem.** All\n   that `n = 2` needed was `#{irreducible monic quadratics} = q(q-1)/2`, and it was obtained by\n   complementation from `#Sym2 K`. At `n = 3` the corresponding input is\n   `#{irreducible monic cubics} = (q³-q)/3`, and the same complementation route\n   (`Sym3`/multiset counting minus the reducible strata) avoids any characteristic case split.\n   Get that count landed EARLY — it is the one piece with no `n = 2` precedent.\n5. **The deep/undecided slack is reusable as-is in shape**: `decided ⊆ certified ∪ deep`,\n   `#deep = o(q^(nN))`. At `n = 3` the pinning argument needs the analogue of `class_pinned`\n   (which `leanfinal` has only at `n = 2`); that is the first thing to check for feasibility,","numLines":62,"startLine":300,"totalLines":363}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e4bf66ce-afd7-4bf5-94e6-a10a264768a2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/data/users/asvin/math-and-lean/p-adic-splitting-densities","sessionId":"525d9ffc-306a-4fb7-9383-b6b9ffb89267","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"main","slug":"abundant-discovering-stallman"}

Three findings were acted\n409\ton:\n410\t* **(G) finding 7 — prose overreach, ACTED ON, and it was a real error.** See the ⚠ block in §4.5\n411\t  and the correction opening §7.\n412\t* **(G) finding 8 — \"axiom-free\" imprecise.** File header and §5 reworded.\n413\t* **(G) finding 9 — \"backportable at reasonable cost\" is a development-history judgement, not a\n414\t  kernel-checkable fact.** File header reworded to say so explicitly.\n415\t\n416\t## 6. OPEN / NOT DONE (recorded honestly, not sorried)\n417\t\n418\t0. **(NOT open — recorded here because the charge asked.)** Uniqueness of the *factorization*\n419\t   LANDED as `monic_factorization_unique`; it did not stall.\n420\t\n421\t1. **Uniqueness of the exact solve (S3).** The map `(u,v) ↦ hu + gv` on\n422\t   `R[X]_{<deg g} × R[X]_{<deg h} → R[X]_{<deg g + deg h}` is bijective, not merely surjective.\n423\t   Injectivity is not proved here. The clean route is: it is a surjective `R`-linear map between\n424\t   finite free `R`-modules of equal rank `n`, hence injective\n425\t   (`Module.Finite`+`OrzechProperty.injective_of_surjective_endomorphism` after transporting along\n426\t   `Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv`). Named open statement:\n427\t   `theorem eq_of_add_mul_eq {g h u v u' v'} (…deg bounds…) : h*u + g*v = h*u' + g*v' → u = u' ∧ v = v'`.\n428\t   The `n = 3` consumer does not obviously need it (uniqueness of the *factorization*, §4.2, is\n429\t   what pinning wants), so it was not pursued.\n430\t2. **The `n`-fold / multi-block form.** \"A pairwise-coprime residual factorization\n431\t   `f̄ = ∏ᵢ p̄ᵢ` lifts to `f = ∏ᵢ pᵢ`\" follows from the two-block form by induction on the number of\n432\t   blocks (the coprimality of `p̄ᵢ` against `∏_{j≠i} p̄ⱼ` is `IsCoprime.prod_right`). Not landed;\n433\t   the `n = 3` branch-(ii) argument only needs two blocks (linear × quadratic).\n434\t3. **The consumer itself.** This unit supplies the *mechanism* named as missing in\n435\t   `N3_CHECK_2026-08-13.md` §7. It does NOT prove branch (ii) of the `n = 3` pinning, and it does\n436\t   not prove `n = 3` drainage. What the consumer still needs is listed in §7 below.\n437\t\n438\t---\n439\t\n440\t## 7. WHAT THE `n = 3` CONSUMER STILL NEEDS — AND A CORRECTION TO `N3_CHECK` §7\n441\t\n442\t**First, the correction (this is the most important paragraph in the note).**\n443\t`N3_CHECK_2026-08-13.md` §7 diagnosed branch (ii) of the `n = 3` pinning argument as *\"blocked on a\n444\tHensel coprime-factorisation lemma\"*, on the grounds that \"the residual repeated factor may be the\n445\tquadratic one\" so the simple-root dodge is unavailable. **At `n = 3` that diagnosis appears to be\n446\twrong, and this unit's own adversarial pass is what exposed it.** Enumerate the residual shapes of\n447\ta cubic that is undecided but NOT triply tangent: the only one is `f̄ = (X − ρ̄)(X − c̄) ^ 2` with\n448\t`ρ̄ ≠ c̄` (the shapes `(X − c̄) ^ 3` is branch (i); every other cubic shape — three distinct roots,\n449\tlinear × irreducible quadratic, irreducible cubic — is decided at level 1 by this repo's own\n450\tcertificates). In that shape `ρ̄` **is** a simple residual root of `f̄`, so mathlib's ROOT form\n451\talready peels it, and the factorization form is not needed for the peel itself.\n452\t\n453\tWhere the factorization form becomes *indispensable* is `n ≥ 4`: e.g. a reduction\n454\t`(X − a) ^ 2 (X − b) ^ 2` with `a ≠ b`, or a product of two distinct irreducible quadratics, has no\n455\tsimple residual root at all, and no amount of root-lifting splits it. So this unit is correctly\n456\tdescribed as **infrastructure for the general theorem**, and only optionally as an `n = 3` unblocker.\n457\t\n458\t**What this unit gives the `n = 3` consumer that the root form does NOT.** Three things, and they\n459\tare the ones a *pinning* argument actually consumes:\n460\t* `isCoprime_of_map_eq` — a Bézout identity `a g + b h = 1` in `O[X]` for the peeled blocks. This is\n461\t  what turns \"`g` divides a product\" into \"`g` divides a factor\", and it does not follow from\n462\t  lifting a root.\n463\t* `monic_factorization_unique` — the peeled pair is the ONLY monic pair with those reductions.\n464\t  Branch (ii)'s injection (\"the factorization is determined by the class\") needs a uniqueness\n465\t  statement; this is its `N = ∞` shadow.\n466\t* `exists_eq_add_mul_of_degree_lt` — exact degree-bounded interpolation, i.e. a concrete CRT\n467\t  splitting `O[X]/(gh) ≅ O[X]/(g) × O[X]/(h)` on representatives, which is the natural home for a\n468\t  coordinatewise counting argument.\n469\t\n470\t**Still missing for branch (ii), and NOT supplied here.**\n471\t1. **The residual trigger.** A lemma turning \"undecided at level `N` and not triply tangent at any\n472\t   centre\" into the residual shape `f̄ = (X − ρ̄)(X − c̄) ^ 2` with `ρ̄ ≠ c̄`. This is a statement\n473\t   about the `n = 3` undecided locus, not about Hensel, and it is where the enumeration in the\n474\t   correction above would have to be made into Lean.\n475\t2. **Class-determinacy at FINITE level.** \"The factorization is determined by the level-`N` class\"\n476\t   needs the quantitative form: if `f ≡ f'` mod `𝔪 ^ N` then the lifted factors agree mod\n477\t   `𝔪 ^ (N − c)` for an explicit `c`. §4.2's uniqueness is only the `N = ∞` shadow of this. The\n478\t   finite-level version is a second induction over the *same* Newton iteration\n479\t   (`exists_solve_step` + `exists_adicLimit_of_degree_lt` are reusable verbatim) and is NOT landed.\n480\t3. **The counting step.** Composing the branch-(ii) injection with the `n = 2` `class_pinned` bound\n481\t   and branch (i)'s triple-tangency Taylor argument into an `undecidedCount_le` at `n = 3`.\n482\t\n483\t---\n484\t\n485\t*Unit note written before the Lean attempt (§§1–2) and completed after it (§§3–7), per the\n486\thouse rule that the informal proof precedes the formalization.*"}]},"uuid":"2aeded13-3cba-47e2-8905-0c297e81a83a","timestamp":"2026-08-13T22:59:57.641Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/data/users/asvin/math-and-lean/p-adic-splitting-densities/leanfinal/notes/HENSEL_FACT_2026-08-13.md","content":"```\n\n---\n\n### 5.1 Independent adversarial pass (Codex, fresh context, 2026-08-13)\n\nThe full file plus a quote-and-classify verifier charge (hunt vacuity, silent weakening,\nmis-binding, definitional traps, prose/statement mismatch; fix nothing) was handed to Codex, which\nhad not seen the design. **Verdict: no critical statement defect.** Findings 1–6 CLEAN\n(generality of `exists_monic_factorization` and a nontrivial witness `R = ℤ_5`, `f = X² − 6`,\n`g₀ = X − 1`, `h₀ = X + 1`; the degree-zero boundary cases in every statement; uniqueness really\nbeing uniqueness of the *ordered* pair; `IsCoprime` being honest Bézout in `R[X]`; exactness and\nthe `u`-against-`h` pairing; `coeffIdeal` having no definitional trap). Every headline below lists which axioms it depends on.\n\n---\n\n## ASSUMED (exhaustive, beyond the 3 Lean-core axioms)\n\n### (A1) The minimal box-Haar / equidistribution axiom — the single irreducible measure residue\n\nCarried as **two structure fields** of `MontesAxiom.MontesData` (NOT a global `axiom`; hypothesis-discharged, so it does NOT surface in `#print axioms`):\n\n- `boxMeasure : CountCell → ℕ → ℚ` — the abstract per-box (p-adic Haar) volume of one cell.\n- `boxHaarEquidist : ∀ c q' > 1, boxMeasure c q' = countCellCoeff c q'`\n  where `countCellCoeff c q = (q^δ)^(dS-1) · bb1Value c.polygon q`.\n  Asserts: the per-box Haar volume **equals** the proved box-volume × residual-count value.\n- `nodeMeasure_boxSum : ∀ T, Tendsto (N ↦ stratumCount T N / q^(nN)) atTop (nhds (Σ_{cells c} boxMeasure c q · ∏_children clusterCount … / countPivot))`\n  Asserts: the node measure **exists** and is the **box-additive** assembly over the cell partition.\n\n**What is assumed** = exactly: (i) the abstract per-box Haar volume IS the proved closed value (box-Haar normalization `T_BB1` + C2 residual equidistribution `T_BB3`), and (ii) the node measure exists and is box-additive. The RHS factors (`bb1Value`, the `(q^δ)^(dS-1)` residual count, the box-additivity arithmetic) are all PROVED (see P1/P2/P3); only the *identification* of the abstract Haar volume with that proved value is assumed.\n\nThis is the genuine **measure wall**: mathlib v4.31.0 has no p-adic Haar measure, so the existence/normalization of `boxMeasure` cannot be constructed in Lean. It is **not** a renamed conclusion and **not** a def-unfold cheat — the asserted equality is to a separately-proved lattice/finite-field value, and the fields assert NO rationality, uniformity, or palindromy.\n\n### (A2) The remaining MontesData / CountingModel structure fields (GMN count shadow, hypotheses)\n\nNone carries rationality / the conclusion:\n- `shapesOf`, `partition` (unique-tree disjoint partition `decidedCount σ N = Σ_T stratumCount T N`);\n- `treeSize`, `cells`, `cells_descend` (strict descent — count shadow of `omCells`/`descend_size_lt`, carried as FIELDS, not the `PadicMeasure` axioms; supplies well-foundedness);\n- `finiteTermination` (GMN Thm 4.18, ≤ n leaves);\n- elementary tail bounds: `undecided_le_split` (≤), `sepTail_tendsto` (separable pool → 0), `discriminantTail_envelope` (q^{-N} root-count envelope) — bounds, NOT the conclusion `U_N → 0` (which is DERIVED, see P6).\n\nThere is **no** `undecided → 0` field and **no** `C_T is rational` field — those are theorems.\n\n### (A3) `tame_functionalEquation` (declared `axiom`, `Interface.lean`)\n\nThe genuine §5 H-tame input: an abstract `DensityFoundation`'s density admits a palindromic rational representative at tame primes. **Only non-core declared axiom** in the headline footprint; appears **only** on `goal_theorem_montes` (and the witness instance), NOT on any pure-rationality constant. Asserts nothing about the count-native `Σ_T C_T` directly — the link is via `hbridge`.\n\n### (A4) `hbridge` (hypothesis argument of `goal_theorem_montes`, NOT an axiom)\n\n`∀ q' > 1, F.density n σ q' = Σ_T coeff T q'`. The honest measure-wall identification (\"abstract foundation density coincides with the count-native OM tree-sum\"). RHS is an arbitrary function; the equality asserts NOTHING about rationality/palindromy/closed form. Introduces no axiom.\n\n### NOT assumed (verified ABSENT from every audited footprint)\n\nThe `PadicMeasure` measure-route axioms — `clusterMeasure`, `AX_cellRecursion`, `AX_columnMeasure`, `omCells`, `descend_size_lt` — are genuine `axiom` declarations in the **dead** `PadicMeasure` module, and are absent from `#print axioms` of `goal_theorem_montes` and of every rationality/decomposition constant.
